learningPath.title: From primordial fluctuations to cosmic structure
learningPath.goal: Connect candidate primordial fluctuations to transfer physics, CMB and large-scale-structure observations, then distinguish measurements from conditional model constraints.
learningPath.prerequisites: Fourier modes and power spectra; introductory quantum fields and homogeneous expanding cosmology.

steps.why: Begin with the proposed accelerated background and the assumptions needed to connect it to the hot Big Bang.
Read the sourced scalar-mode and power-spectrum formulas. Distinguish their assumed initial state from an observation of that state.
Identify the model-dependent transition to the thermal era. This is a pedagogical checkpoint, not a claim that resonant preheating is required or observed.
Use the transfer primer to connect primordial initial conditions to the late-time background and linear observables; then open the existing Planck, BK18 and DESI Evidence records.

primer.title: The bridge: initial conditions, transfer and inference

paragraphs.text: Separate the stages: inflationary dynamics specifies a candidate primordial spectrum; transfer physics predicts later sky and matter statistics; a likelihood compares those predictions with data. This is a study sequence, not a proof that one inflationary mechanism occurred.

The existing Mukhanov–Sasaki and slow-roll formulas concern initial scalar perturbations, not the full subsequent plasma evolution. Their canonical single-field, Einstein-gravity, spatially flat assumptions and the adiabatic super-Hubble conservation condition must remain explicit.

The missing transfer layer is explained here without adding a new theory node. Ma–Bertschinger evolves linear scalar perturbations in flat backgrounds using synchronous or conformal Newtonian gauge: CDM and baryons as fluids, photons and massless/massive neutrinos kinetically. Their isentropic super-horizon initial conditions are an assumption, not all possible initial states. Density contrasts require a specified gauge; observable anisotropies cannot depend on that coordinate choice.

Photons scatter before recombination and then propagate to us. Line-of-sight integration combines the evolving source with geometrical projection to predict CMB multipoles. Matter transfer instead describes species-dependent density evolution. Linear transfer is not a complete nonlinear galaxy-formation model; galaxy clustering needs additional observational and modeling treatment.

Planck primordial-spectrum constraints are inferred from temperature, polarization and lensing data under specified models. BK18 provides a tensor upper limit with foreground modeling, not a primordial-wave detection. Neither identifies the inflaton or demonstrates primordial quantum coherence. The scalar transfer discussion does not by itself calculate tensor B modes.

DESI DR2 BAO measures distance ratios relative to the sound horizon; absolute distances require a calibration. It is not a direct image of the inflaton. Keep BAO-only results distinct from CMB/supernova combinations and their parameterization-dependent dark-energy constraints. These dated records are not claims to be the latest available limits.

record.evidenceNote: Guth–Pi calculates density perturbations from quantum-field fluctuations in a specific new-inflation model (its amplitude was too large); the reviewed canonical single-field calculation provides the broader qualified route. Direction means background dynamics supplies a setting for fluctuation generation, not that every inflation model has identical predictions.

record.note: Conditional initial-spectrum input to structure predictions; not proof of inflation.
record.evidenceNote: Source-grounded synthesis: A candidate primordial spectrum supplies initial statistical input for linear Einstein–Boltzmann evolution and projection in a specified cosmological model. The direction records this conditional input-to-prediction role, not logical entailment of Lambda-CDM, historical descent, or empirical confirmation of an inflationary mechanism. Post-inflation transfer is not identical to Mukhanov–Sasaki dynamics.
